description: Independent data investigations built from public data. Each Data Note interrogates one dataset — with original charts, a clear argument, and an honest account of what the numbers can and can't show.

data_dives.title: Almost all of India’s export growth came from services
data_dives.tagline: India's total exports rose $42.80 billion in 2024-25. Merchandise contributed $0.35 billion of it; services contributed $42.45 billion. The goods deficit hit a record $282.83 billion, and the services surplus covered two-thirds of it.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data
sections: The gap, and what covers it
One side moved, the other did not

data_dives.title: Most of what India borrows pays for what it already borrowed
data_dives.tagline: The 2026-27 Budget borrows ₹16.96 lakh crore and pays ₹14.04 lakh crore in interest — 83 paise in the rupee, up from 71 two years ago. Plus: why the famous budget-rupee pie and the budget table do not use the same rupee.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: Announced, unspent, announced again
data_dives.tagline: India budgeted ₹10.49 lakh crore for centrally sponsored schemes in 2025-26 and revised it to ₹8.46 lakh crore. Four flagship schemes lost 70–85% of their allocation in-year, then received almost the same number again.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data
sections: One number that looks like a cut and is not

data_dives.title: The states’ 41% share comes to 35% of the tax
data_dives.tagline: The Sixteenth Finance Commission kept the states’ share of central taxes at 41%. In 2026-27 states receive ₹15.26 lakh crore of the ₹44.04 lakh crore collected — 34.7%. The difference is everything that sits outside the divisible pool.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: The wage that ran to stand still
data_dives.tagline: India's MGNREGA wage has roughly quadrupled on paper since 2006 and barely moved in real terms. Indexed only to prices, it now sits below the state minimum wage across much of the country.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data
sections: Quadrupled on paper, flat in real terms
Below the floor the state sets itself

data_dives.title: The states that spend most on welfare have the least to show for it
data_dives.tagline: India's biggest social-sector spenders record its worst welfare outcomes, while the states that spend the least pull ahead. What the RBI's 2025-26 state-budget data really shows — and what it can't.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: The women dropping off the voter list
data_dives.tagline: When India revised its electoral rolls, women were deleted in far greater numbers than men — and the documents demanded fall hardest on women. The gendered edge of the Special Intensive Revision.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: Whose name is on the house?
data_dives.tagline: India's housing scheme puts homes in women's names by mandate — up to 97% of them. Yet only 42% of women own a house at all, and just 13% in their sole name. The gap between the paperwork and the deed.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: Paid an honorarium, not a wage
data_dives.tagline: India runs its nutrition and rural-health systems on ~34 lakh women paid a central 'honorarium' of ₹4,500 a month or less — below the wage floor. Calling the work voluntary is what keeps it cheap.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: The safety fund nobody spends
data_dives.tagline: India's Nirbhaya Fund for women's safety is either 76% spent or barely a fifth spent, depending on what you divide by. How one fund produces three official utilisation figures — and where the money sits.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data

data_dives.title: The pension that never got a raise
data_dives.tagline: India's central old-age pension has been ₹200 a month since 2006. Inflation cut its real value by two-thirds; what an elderly person actually receives now depends mostly on which state they live in.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data
sections: The flat line and the falling line

data_dives.title: Thirty-seven threat groups, and nothing to divide them by
data_dives.tagline: Anthropic's September 2026 threat report names 37 distinct threat groups disrupted over eight months. Surveillance accounts for ten, more than cyber. The number is real, checkable, and cannot be read as a rate.
data_dives.author: ImpactMojo Data
sections: What is actually in the report
The two columns do not track each other
Why you cannot divide by anything
Read it as a typology, not as a measurement
